subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219's derived setup watchdog policy as the canonical fix for this generic isolated-cron setup-timeout class?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes default availability behavior by letting pre-runner setup hold a cron slot longer than the current fixed 60s ceiling.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Land the 60s floor, half-job-timeout, 10-minute-cap approach and keep operator configurability or backend-specific fixes separate.

options.title: Require a configurable watchdog
options.body: Ask for an explicit cron config surface and docs before merge, accepting more config complexity to give operators direct control.

options.title: Keep the fixed 60s ceiling
options.body: Reject the longer setup window and instead require deeper setup-phase diagnostics or backend-specific fixes before changing timeout policy.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the 60s floor, half-job-timeout, 10-minute-cap approach and keep operator configurability or backend-specific fixes separate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history and release ownership touch the cron watchdog/timer files most directly involved in this policy tradeoff.
